quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

33 Questions • Passing Score 27

questions.question: You are driving in the right lane of a multilane highway and want to move into the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check both mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Always signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection with no stop sign or traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving at the same speed.
Stop, look in all directions, and then go.
Yield to all other drivers.
Be ready to yield if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield if needed.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control, yield to vehicles coming from the right. Always be ready to yield by taking your foot off the gas, getting ready to brake, and looking left, right, and left again.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: Merging traffic ahead.
Drive carefully and stay alert.
Pedestrians are crossing.
Stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully and stay alert.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive with caution.

questions.question: What are stop lines?

options.text: White lines painted on curves and hills.
White lines painted near churches and schools.
Solid white lines at intersections and crosswalks.
White lines on freeway ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Solid white lines at intersections and crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes at intersections and crosswalks. They show where you must stop.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When driving through an intersection.
When passing a bicyclist.
When a child is about to run into the street.
When parallel parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a child is about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. For example, honk if a child is about to run into the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Press hard on the brakes.
Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not slam on the brakes. Hold the steering wheel tightly and stay in your lane. Slow down by releasing the gas pedal. When you are going very slowly, gently apply the brakes and move off the road to a safe area.

questions.question: What is an inattentive driver?

options.text: A driver who stares at things off the road or daydreams.
A driver who looks at passengers instead of the road.
A driver who only watches the car in front.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by passengers, looking for items in your car, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming. Keep scanning the road, checking mirrors, and watching your instruments regularly. These habits keep you alert.

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your car and the car in front?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
When exiting a highway.
When following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance behind large vehicles that block your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting a highway, when following a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: You are driving in another driver's blind spot. What should you do?

options.text: Move ahead or drop back so the driver can see you.
Keep driving at the same speed.
Stay in the blind spot.
Honk your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move ahead or drop back so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Never drive in someone else's blind spot. Move forward or backward so that driver can see you.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Speed up.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Intersection ahead.
Four-way stop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is coming. Watch carefully for traffic crossing in front of you.

questions.question: An oncoming driver does not dim their high beam headlights. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the oncoming vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded by the headlights and helps you see the road until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use your:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Hazard flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights if your vehicle has them. High beams bounce off the fog and reflect into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:

options.text: Flashing red light.
Steady yellow light.
Yellow arrow.
Flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look both ways, and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." This means:

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
You should reduce your speed to 35 mph only when weather is bad.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: When you see a "Reduced speed" sign with a speed limit, the new speed limit begins at that sign.

questions.question: To enter a freeway:

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as other vehicles.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, signal and match the speed of traffic. Always yield to other vehicles when entering.

questions.question: To be ready for hazards ahead, you should:

options.text: Look at the entire road and all sides of the road.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Keep your focus on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and all sides of the road.
questions.explanation: Handling dangerous situations depends on spotting problems early. Scan the entire road, including both sides, not just the center.

questions.question: Traffic moving in opposite directions is divided by ____ lines.

options.text: White
Red
Black
Yellow

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: You may go carefully through an intersection with a yellow light if:

options.text: An emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
Pedestrians are crossing.
You are turning right.
You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in an intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through carefully.

questions.question: You should use extra caution near a pedestrian with a white cane because:

options.text: He or she is deaf.
He or she is a police officer.
He or she is blind.
He or she has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: He or she is blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane means the person is blind. Slow down, yield, and be ready to stop to avoid hitting them.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by a strong adult.
Will be safe standing on the floor in the back.
Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never stand while the vehicle is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never stand while the vehicle is moving.
questions.explanation: Children must always be in proper car seats or safety seats. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Children must be properly restrained at all times.

questions.question: What should a driver do if they see an animal on the road?

options.text: No special action is needed.
The driver should honk their horn.
The driver should pass the animal as close as possible.
The driver should be very careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver should be very careful.
questions.explanation: Always be careful when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly so you don't startle or scare it.

questions.question: When must headlights be used?

options.text: Only when traffic is very heavy.
During all of daylight savings time.
From half an hour before sunset to half an hour after sunrise.
From half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise.

questions.correctAnswerText: From half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise.
questions.explanation: You must use headlights between half an hour after sunset and half an hour before sunrise. You must also use them anytime you cannot see at least 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Take a different route.
Drive the same way you would on dry roads.
Stay farther back from the car in front of you.
Avoid all bridges and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back from the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between you and the car ahead. Your vehicle will need more time to stop than it would on dry roads.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for drunk drivers.
There are curves ahead.
The road is slippery when wet.
Apply your brakes quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that the road can be slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: What is a shared center lane on a two-way road used for?

options.text: Making left turns only.
Making U-turns, where allowed.
Vehicles traveling in both directions.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Shared center lanes are used for left turns and U-turns where allowed. Both directions of traffic can use these lanes.

questions.question: What should you do when an oncoming car is on your left and a bicyclist is on your right?

options.text: Drive onto the shoulder.
Split the difference between them.
Let the car pass first, then pass the bicycle.
Pass the bicycle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass first, then pass the bicycle.
questions.explanation: Deal with one danger at a time. Let the oncoming car pass. Then pass the bicycle. Do not try to squeeze between both at the same time.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop when a flagger tells you to stop at a railroad crossing.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing lights and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered crossing gates.

questions.question: What must you do when a transit bus signals to return to the main road after a stop?

options.text: Honk to let them know you are there.
Move to the left lane.
Let them merge in front of you.
Speed up to pass them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them merge in front of you.
questions.explanation: You must let a transit bus merge back into traffic after it has stopped. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to give the bus room to enter safely.

questions.question: Is checking your blind spot before changing lanes a good driving habit?

options.text: No, it is a bad habit.
Yes, it is a good habit.
No, it is not necessary.
No, mirrors are enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is a good habit.
questions.explanation: Always check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with sirens and flashing lights approaches you?

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights and sirens approaches, immediately drive to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light ahead is red.
The traffic light ahead is broken.
The traffic light ahead is green.
A traffic light is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A traffic light is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic light is at the next intersection.

questions.question: Traffic signals use arrows to control turns from specific lanes. What does a green arrow mean?

options.text: It is only used on one-way streets.
It means go, and you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may proceed only if a green arrow appears with a green circle light.
It shows the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means go, and you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. You must turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Turn on your flashers.
Pull to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull to the side of the road and stop immediately.
